line_recommendation: Recent sales, adjusted to your home, support {low} to {high}, with a median adjusted value of {median}. {price} sits {position}, {vs}.
line_range_override: This range is our judgment rather than the standard method's {rule}: {reason}
pos_bottom: near the bottom of the range
pos_middle: in the middle of the range
pos_top: near the top of the range
history_reprice: Listed at {current} for {days} days without a sale.

history_relist_cut: The earlier listing started at {original}, was cut to {failed} and ended unsold{after}.
history_listed_cut: The listing started at {original}, was cut to {failed} and didn't sell{after}.

history_pending_cut: The listing started at {original}, was cut to {failed} and went under contract{after}, but the sale didn't close.
line_comps_count: These are the {n} closest matches, sold {first} to {last}{since}{within}.
line_comps_summary: Adjusted to your home, these sales run from {lo} to {hi}, with a median of {median}.
line_strongest: The strongest match is {address}: the smallest adjustments among the sales inside the supported range.
line_highest: The highest sale among them is {address} at {price}{when}; a contract well above the supported range invites a low appraisal.
h_scatter: Where Your Home Fits in the Neighborhood
line_scatter_intro: Every recent sale and listing in the MLS records from {lo} to {hi} square feet, plotted by size and price, with the comparable sales in color and your home at the recommended price.
trend_head_above: At {price}, your home sits about {gap} above what its size alone predicts.
trend_head_below: At {price}, your home sits about {gap} below what its size alone predicts.
trend_head_at: At {price}, your home sits about where its size alone predicts.
trend_caption: The dashed line shows what homes here sell for based on size alone. Homes above it sold for more, usually because of condition, updates or the lot.
trend_above: Your home's condition and features have to justify the difference.
trend_below: Buyers comparing homes by size will see it as a good value.
line_r2: Size explains {share} of the price differences here.
excluded_size_one: One home far larger or smaller than yours is left off the chart.
excluded_size_many: {n} homes far larger or smaller than yours are left off the chart.
excluded_price_one: One home priced far from what its size predicts is left off the chart and out of the dashed line.
excluded_price_many: {n} homes priced far from what their size predicts are left off the chart and out of the dashed line.

mk_sale_to_list: Typical Sale vs. Original Asking Price
mk_days: Typical Days to Go Under Contract

h_payments: What Your Price Means to Buyers
pay_intro: Buyers shop by monthly payment. Each $10,000 in price changes a typical buyer's payment by about {per10k} a month and the down payment by {down10k}.
line_sources_export: Sales and listings: MLS records, {n} sales from {first} to {last}, {listings}.
line_sources_listings: plus {active} active, {pending} pending and {ended} expired, withdrawn or canceled listings
line_sources_comps: Sales: the comparable sales named in this report, from the MLS.
line_sources_rate: Mortgage rate: {rate}, the Freddie Mac weekly survey for {date}.
line_shelf_life: Markets change, so this analysis should be refreshed if the home isn't listed within a few weeks.
note_expected_export: Expected sales are estimates, not guarantees: each option's list price times {ratio}, what nearby homes sold since {since} got against their final asking price after seller-paid costs, plus that option's seller credit, to the nearest $500.
note_expected_report: Expected sales are estimates, not guarantees: each option's list price times {ratio}, what the sales we reviewed got against their final asking price after seller-paid costs, plus that option's seller credit, to the nearest $500.
note_expected_assumed: Expected sales are estimates, not guarantees: each option's list price times an assumed {ratio} of its final asking price after seller-paid costs, plus that option's seller credit, to the nearest $500.
note_expected_limits: None is below the supported range (the comps are already net of seller credits) or above its list price or the top of the range.
note_expected_top: At {prices} we expect the recommended option's sale: a price above the range usually sells after a cut, so it costs time rather than adding to the sale.
note_expected_agent: The {prices} option's expected sale is our own estimate.
note_expected_agent_many: The {prices} options' expected sales are our own estimates.
note_expected_stay: Staying at the current price expects what recent sales that sat as long got against their original asking price.
note_competing: The {price} net assumes competing offers; without them it likely nets less.
note_holding: Holding costs: about {monthly} a month ({loan}) from the report date to each option's closing; property tax is in the proration.
note_holding_loan_rate: loan interest at the seller's {rate} rate on the {payoff} payoff
note_holding_loan_assumed: loan interest on the {payoff} payoff at an assumed {rate} a year
note_holding_no_loan: no loan interest, since there's no mortgage
note_holding_loan_unknown: no loan interest, since no mortgage payoff was given
note_tax_closing: Each option's property tax proration runs from Jan 1 to its own expected closing.
note_tax_next_year: The {options} option closes in {next}, so it also pays this year's whole bill (assumed unpaid) plus {next}'s share to closing.
note_tax_next_year_many: The {options} options close in {next}, so they also pay this year's whole bill (assumed unpaid) plus {next}'s share to closing.
note_tax_unpaid: This year's tax bill is assumed still unpaid at closing, so the seller's share is credited to the buyer; if the seller pays the bill first, the buyer credits back the rest of the year instead.
note_title_fees: Title company fees are typical local charges ({items}); the title company's quote replaces them.
note_national: Estimates, not local figures: {items}. Local rates or a title quote replace them.
note_payoff: The mortgage payoff is the seller's estimate; the lender's payoff statement gives the final figure.
note_payoff_balance: The mortgage payoff is estimated from the loan balance plus a month's interest; the lender's payoff statement gives the final figure.
note_commission_default: Brokerage is at the default rates ({items}), shown with no label: ask for the listing agreement's terms, which replace them.
note_commission_default_reprice: Brokerage is at the default rates ({items}), shown with no label. This is the agent's own listing, so the listing agreement already sets the commission: ask for its terms.
note_not_included: Not included: {items}. The closing agent provides the exact figures.
not_included_tax: this year's property tax proration (the tax bill and the expected closing date add it)
note_state_unknown: No state or county for this home, so the nets use national estimates and the report is Preliminary. The MLS records come from {mls} MLS, built in for {state}: if this is {state}, the net sheet uses {line} instead of {estimate}, and the recommended option nets {amount} {way}. Ask for the city and county.
pay_note: Buyer payments: {program} loan, {down} down, {rate} 30-year fixed, property taxes at {basis}, {ins} a year {ins_kind}{mi}.
pay_note_tax_estimated: Buyer taxes are estimated at {basis}: no millage for this area yet.
pay_no_homestead: Taxes assume no homestead exemption; a buyer who files one would pay less.
pay_no_homestead_built_in: Taxes assume no homestead exemption (none is built in for this state); a buyer who files one would pay less.
